sources.title: Majority-vote writer fixture plus actual-candidate exhaustive independent oracle

claims.text: The preserved source asks for a strict-majority number using Boyer-Moore voting, without specifying an API or explicit majority-exists guarantee.
The actual candidate uses Boyer-Moore cancellation to select a candidate and a second linear pass to verify the strict-majority condition when existence is not guaranteed.
Independent exhaustive and boundary checks reject exact-half/no-majority inputs and accept only occurrences strictly greater than n/2.
The implementation performs at most two linear scans while storing only candidate and counters, matching O(n) time and O(1) extra algorithm space.

validation.command: writer randomized fixture plus independently compiled actual-candidate exhaustive oracle
validation.reported_stdout: PASS writer randomized=20000; PASS actual candidate exhaustive=29524 + boundaries

boundary_tests.expected: exact half and no-majority rejected; > n/2 accepted
match independent HashMap oracle for every length 0..9 array over {-1,0,1}
negative majority supported without sentinel collision

findings: The exact repository source asks for a number occurring more than half the time and names Boyer-Moore voting; it does not specify an API or explicitly guarantee that such an element always exists.
The candidate keeps the missing existence guarantee explicit and therefore separates candidate selection from a second-pass strict-majority verification instead of silently assuming success.
The explanation correctly uses strict > n/2 semantics; an exact-half case is not accepted.
The cancellation argument explains why a true strict majority survives pairwise cancellation while also explaining why an unverified survivor is insufficient when no majority exists.

An independently authored exhaustive oracle compiles and runs the actual candidate over every length 0..9 array on a three-value alphabet, plus null, empty, singleton, exact-half, no-majority and negative-value boundaries.
The O(n) time and O(1) extra-space claims match the two linear scans and constant algorithm state; the optional return contract is explicitly answer-side.
No project experience is fabricated; the answer marks production/API choices as implementation policy rather than preserved source facts.
